note: DECLARED, NOT PROVEN - and therefore not launchable; every route naming this descriptor refuses at preflight with HARNESS_BINDING_UNPROVEN. WHAT BLOCKS IT, exactly: `codex-cli 0.147.0` IS installed on deployment #0 as of 2026-08-14 (it was not when worker-harness-core wrote its report on 2026-08-13, and its arrival mid-task is why this file was rewritten), but `codex login status` reports NOT LOGGED IN. No model call is possible, so the deny-enforced and allow-executes probes cannot run and no class can be proven through the real agent loop. That is one operator act away, not a redesign. FLAG NAMES HERE ARE OBSERVED, from `codex exec --help` and `codex sandbox --help` on the installed 0.147.0, not copied from documentation - an earlier draft of this file named `--ask-for-approval never`, which does not exist on `codex exec` in this build, and that is exactly the class of error a declared descriptor is supposed to be suspected of. WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED is stated per class below rather than smoothed over, and one retraction belongs up front: an earlier draft asserted that Codex has no per-command allow/deny list at all. That claim is withdrawn. `codex exec --ignore-rules` is documented by the binary itself as `Do not load user or project execpolicy .rules files`, so an execpolicy mechanism exists; its file format, scope resolution, and whether it can express a per-path READ denial were not established here, and P2's residual says so.

classes.title: the access layer is never touched from a worker

mechanisms.detail: OBSERVED to exist as a flag on `codex exec` with exactly the three values in known_command_modes. DECLARED, UNMEASURED: that the sandbox actually refuses a privileged operation. The binary ships its own Linux sandbox helper and bundles `bwrap`, so the mechanism is an OS-level confinement rather than a command matcher - which is a different and in principle stronger shape than the Claude Code row, and the reason this table compares outcomes rather than syntax

OBSERVED: `Do not load $CODEX_HOME/config.toml; auth still uses CODEX_HOME`. This is Codex's exact analogue of Claude Code's --setting-sources gating - the boundary does not depend on the operator's global config and their global config cannot widen it, while authentication still resolves. It is the single most important flag in this row and it was found by reading the installed binary's help, not by inference

probes.note: cannot be run: the harness is present but not authenticated. Note this probe is written in the same harmless-canary form the Claude Code row uses, which will be WRONG for Codex if its boundary turns out to be an OS sandbox rather than a command matcher - an `echo` naming sudo would sail through a sandbox that would still refuse the real call. Whoever proves this row must decide the probe form from Codex's actual mechanism, not copy this one.

classes.residual: Unmeasured, in both directions. A sandbox that confines writes is not automatically one that refuses a privileged call, and a sandbox that refuses one may refuse it by failing rather than by denying, which is a different fact to record.

classes.title: secrets are never read, never printed, never committed

mechanisms.detail: ENFORCEABLE, PROVEN, AND NOT VENDOR-DEPENDENT: the child's environment is constructed by this launcher's own adapter from an allowlist, and any addition whose name looks credential-shaped is refused at the adapter boundary. This half of P2 binds on Codex exactly as it binds on Claude Code, because the launcher owns it rather than the harness - and it is covered by the same tests
WORKER.md plus review, for the printing surface no matcher expresses

classes.residual: THE NAMED GAP, and it is now a narrower and more honest gap than the first draft claimed. What is established: the environment half binds, and it binds here. What is NOT established: whether Codex can express a per-path READ denial equivalent to Claude Code's Read(**/*.env). Its sandbox is documented to scope writes and network; an execpolicy `.rules` mechanism demonstrably exists (`--ignore-rules` names it), and whether a rule can deny a read - or gates only shell invocations - was not determined. So this descriptor claims only the environment half, and closing the rest needs either a Codex control established by measurement or an already-approved isolation layer around the worker root. That is an operator decision and is not taken here. This class alone is enough reason for the route to refuse.

classes.title: the durable stack is never mutated, and shared infrastructure is never destroyed

mechanisms.detail: DECLARED: writes outside the workspace root are denied at the OS layer, which would cover the container-runtime and multiplexer sockets that P3's incidents ran through - the effect of destroying a multiplexer is a write to a server socket outside the workspace. UNMEASURED: whether that socket path is in fact outside the sandbox's writable set on this host
OBSERVED: the operator's config.toml cannot relax the sandbox mode this launch pins

probes.note: a placeholder, deliberately inert. The real probe for this row cannot be written until the mechanism is known: against an OS sandbox the meaningful test is an attempted WRITE outside the workspace root, which `codex sandbox` can run deterministically with no model call and no tokens once a permission profile exists. That is the cheap path to proving this row and it is left to whoever holds the credential.

classes.residual: Unmeasured. The socket-path reasoning above is inference from documented sandbox behaviour, not a reading of what this build does.

classes.title: the network is reached through named tools, not raw fetches

mechanisms.detail: DECLARED: network access is documented as disabled by default under this sandbox mode, which would close P4 STRUCTURALLY rather than by naming curl and wget. If that holds it is materially stronger than the Claude Code row, whose command matcher is evadable by obfuscation. UNMEASURED here

probes.note: a placeholder. A real network-denial probe must be run by someone who is permitted to attempt a network call; the author of this descriptor is bound by P4 and did not route around it through the sandbox.

classes.residual: If network is off wholesale, the POSITIVE half of P4 needs measuring too: git over https and package installs must still work, or the route is bound and useless. That trade is what a probe run settles and no document can. Codex also exposes an allowed-domains/proxy configuration surface, which may make this a partial rather than binary answer.
